meaning: In the verification pulse-amplitude table, a missing amplitude is printed as "n/a" and any value is rounded to 3 decimals. It is a display-only formatter inside the printout, not part of the fit objective.

could_move.what: The printed amplitude table: digits shown, and beats with no computed amplitude shown as "n/a" instead of a number
Whether an "n/a" hides a genuinely failed amplitude call (no detected beats in that window) rather than a benign gap; the table cannot distinguish the two
Reading of the limit-cycle vs old-seed baseline gap, which is the stated purpose of this table
Amplitude panels in patient decks using the same routine could disagree with the table's rounding

expectation: Unknown in magnitude. Most likely no effect on fitted parameters, since this sits in a println path; the visible effect is the printed digits and the placeholder. I cannot rule out from this context that the same formatting is reused elsewhere.

check.why: Lists every caller of the amplitude routine and every other "n/a" placeholder, so you can see whether this formatting is display-only or feeds something else, without re-running a fit.
